Kawasaki plans North American launch of the 110-kg CP110L palletizer

The regional debut is scheduled for PACK EXPO, with its 2,200-case-per-hour rating tied to specified payload and motion conditions.

Kawasaki Robotics ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A regional rollout milestone

Kawasaki Robotics USA announced on October 8 that the CP110L would make its North American debut at PACK EXPO in Chicago on October 18–21. This is a regional rollout following the global launch on February 16. The target applications are packaging and end-of-line operations constrained by floor space and ceiling height.

Payload and speed are different ratings

The four-axis robot has a maximum payload of 110 kilograms, a 2,505-mm reach and ±0.05-mm repeatability. The 2,200-case-per-hour rating applies at 60 kilograms including the gripper, using a motion pattern with a 400-mm rise, 2,000-mm horizontal travel and 400-mm descent. It is not a guaranteed rate at maximum payload or in every cell layout.

Compact architecture still needs integration

Kawasaki specifies a required ceiling height of 2,242 mm and a revolute-axis interference radius of 453 mm. A hollow wrist routes cables and hoses internally, while regeneration reuses energy from deceleration. The robot weighs 820 kilograms, so integrators still need to validate mounting, tooling, safety clearances and actual cycle times. Regional pricing was not announced.
